item.title: Roadblocks — Thu Nov 12, 6:00 PM — Studio Montclair Leach Gallery
item.description: “Roadblocks,” an exhibition that delves into the concept of the barriers—both physical and metaphorical—that shape our societies and lives as individuals. The works in this exhibit explore—with diversity and breadth–how roadblocks are constructed, perceived, and sometimes dismantled. 2D, 3D, photographic, and digital artworks examine the ways in which the barriers in our lives often hinder connection, understanding, and progress and yet can ultimately foster positive growth. Augmenting this exhibit will be a thought-provoking Zoom Webinar on Wednesday, November 18 at 7pm featuring guest speakers who will, through selected artworks, delve into the tangible and abstract barriers that shape our societies, relationships, and identities as individuals. Hosted by exhibit jurors Lisa D’Amico and Debbie Silberberg, the conversation will feature special guest speakers Naomi Vladeck, artists’ life coach, and Jose Perez, artist and psychotherapist. item.title: Beyond Cornell: What the Research Tells Us About Sex Education, Consent, and Safer Communities — Fri Nov 13, 8:00 AM — Montclair Women’s Club
item.description:
Join Dr. Eva Goldfarb, Professor of Public Health at Montclair State University, for a compelling, evidence-based discussion on why comprehensive sex education is essential for building healthier, safer communities. Dr. Goldfarb is the lead author of a landmark study demonstrating that comprehensive sex education does far more than reduce unintended pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections. It strengthens communication skills, healthy relationships, and reduces sexual violence. Dr. Goldfarb will discuss these findings as well as her recent research on sexual consent, offering important insights into why what we teach in our schools (and at home) matters long before students reach college. item.description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed for adults who regularly interact with young people ages 12–18. It teaches parents, caregivers, family members, teachers, school staff, and other caring adults how to recognize and respond to mental health or substance use challenges and support a young person who may be experiencing a crisis. The Course will:
Introduce common mental health challenges for youth Review typical adolescent development Teach a 5-step action plan for how to help young people in both crisis and non-crisis situations
Participants will receive certification after completion of all pre and post work, as well as 4 live virtual training sessions. Registration closes 11/10.

item.title: Chamber Opera Performance: "L'enfant et les Sortilèges" — Sun Dec 6, 5:00 PM — Alexander Kasser Theater
item.description:
Maurice Ravel’s L’enfant et les sortilèges is a wildly imaginative fantasy opera where a single child’s tantrum sets an entire enchanted world into motion. In a flash of frustration, the ordinary becomes extraordinary—walls start to whisper, teacups burst into song, animals argue back, and the child’s room transforms into a living, breathing world of magic and mischief. As this fantastical realm awakens, the child is swept into a dazzling swirl of musical surprises and unexpected voices, where every object has something to say and nothing is quite as it seems. With Ravel’s shimmering, kaleidoscopic score at its heart, this enchanting opera is a playful journey through wonder, chaos, and the power of imagination to transform everything it touches. (Sung in French with English Surtitles~ runtime: approx 1 hour) Montclair State University Students FREE with ID at Kasser Box Office
Hosted by: The College of the Arts

item.title: The "Blues" – A History of the 20th Century's Most Influential Folk Music — Mon Jan 25, 6:00 PM — Glen Ridge - Meeting Room
item.description:
The Blues was a form of regional Black Folk Music composed of African rhythms, the musical structure of the English/ Scottish song, the acoustic guitar and the Black version of the English language. It is generally, but not exclusively, associated with the Mississippi-Yazoo Delta’s cotton plantation workers, those that built the levees along the Mississippi, the stevedores and the convicts from the penitentiaries.
Join 20th century music expert, John Groom, as he explores the early roots of the Blues and the way it has influenced music and culture for generations.

item.description:
Run Time: 80 minutes, no intermission
In 2021, Sydney comedian Sam Kissajukian decided to quit standup, rent an abandoned cake factory, and become a painter. Over the course of a six-month manic episode, he created 300 large-scale paintings, unknowingly documenting his mental state through the process. In this hilarious, fascinating, and wildly original show, Kissajukian brings audiences on a rollercoaster ride that explores the ties between art, mental health, and creativity. Each performance includes post-show access to an art exhibit featuring Kissajukian and his works.
“Beautifully frank.” (The New Yorker)

item.description:
For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.
A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.
The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.
The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.
This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.
